title: A research study investigating denecimig (Mim8) in adults with acquired haemophilia A
official: A multinational, open-label study to investigate efficacy and safety of denecimig (Mim8) in adults with acquired haemophilia A
summary: Main objective: To confirm the haemostatic effect of denecimig as bleeding prophylaxis in adults with acquired haemophilia A, by demonstrating that the upper bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval for the weekly bleeding rate is < CCI bleeds per participant week
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Informed consent obtained before any study-related activities. Study-related activities are any procedures that are carried out as part of the study, including activities to determine suitability for the study.
2. 2. Male or female participants (sex assigned at birth, inclusive of all gender identities) newly diagnosed with AHA prior to signing the informed consent form, with AHA diagnosis (FVIII activity <50% and FVIII inhibitors >0.6 BU) confirmed at screening.
3. 3. Treatment-requiring bleed(s) due to AHA from diagnosis and until screening.
4. 4. The participant is capable of following study procedures and able to seek medical attention when needed.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Female who is pregnant, breast-feeding or intends to become pregnant or is of childbearing potential and not using an adequate and highly effective contraceptive method.
2. 2. Previous or current thromboembolic disease or events (with the exception of previous catheter associated thrombosis for which anti-thrombotic treatment is not currently ongoing) or risk of thromboembolic disease.
3. 3. Life expectancy <3 months at the time of screening, as evaluated by the investigator.
4. 4. Therapy with immunosuppressive or immune modulating drugs for treatment of AHA (other than ≤2 days of prednisolone (or equivalent) for AHA at a dose ≤100 mg per day), prior to screening.  - IST initiated prior to AHA diagnosis for other medical conditions (e.g., other autoimmune disorders) is permitted, provided it was intitiated ≥6 months prior to screening, has been maintained at a stable dose  and regimen since initiation, and is expected  to remain at a stable dose and regimen at least during main treatment period (Weeks 0-12).
